items.title: Battleground Cleaner Simulator Announced for PC
items.summary:
When army-sized battles rage in stuff like Game of Thrones, someone has to clean up the mess afterwards. That's the premise behind Battleground Cleaner Simulator, which tasks you with tidying up after chaotic medieval events like battlefields, drunken tavern brawls, and feasts that leave blood all over the castle, bodies with forks in their eyes, and so, so much more. 

Developed by Mad Muffin Studios and published by Garden of Dreams, Battleground Cleaner Simulator is a very unserious game in the best (and funniest) of ways, as you'll see when you take a look at the trailer above. You'll play as a lowly servant tasked with cleaning up the aftermath of various gone-too-far events in the times of knights and kings. You must scrub the blood off the walls, floors, and furniture, pick up and dispose of the bodies (some of which might have kitchen utensils jammed in their eye sockets), and generally just restore the place to being spotless – lest the ruling class get dissatisfied and decide to dispose of you too.

"Work quietly, keep your mouth shut, and make sure everything looks as if nothing ever happened," Mad Muffin Studios describes. "Your clients are generous — but they don’t take kindly to loose tongues."

There's no release date for Battleground Cleaner Simulator just yet, so you might want to wishlist it on Steam to keep track of it as development progresses.

She made a brief appearance in GTA 6 Trailer 1, released back in 2023, and it sparked a bunch of fan theories that she was actually Lucia, just heavily customised. items.title: GTA 6 Players Are Refusing to Make Use of an Infinite Money Glitch They Say Ruins the Experience
items.summary:
Players have already found ways to farm infinite money, undermining the carefully paced economy of GTA 6 using multiple methods. While this happens with every game, it’s particularly strange here. 

Why is it weird? GTA 6 already has infinite money. You can rob as many stores and businesses as you like and fence the goods, and while stores close down for a while after they’ve been robbed, they reset on a frequent basis.

You just have to play as intended, but some players are hellbent on farming cash in the most mind-numbing ways possible. The methods are all built around forcing the store closure timers to reset, so you can rob the same stores on repeat. 

First, they rob a bunch of stores and collect as much as possible, then they trigger a mission to start a cutscene. Once the cutscene begins, they restart the mission from the menu. When the cutscene begins again, they quit out of the mission, which forces all the stores to reset. 

Honestly, it sounds arduous and you’d be better off exploring to find new robbery opportunities so you can experience fresh gameplay. 

Another method sees players go to a lucrative building, get all of the money and narcotics from inside, and store them in the trunk of their car. Next they save the game and immediately load it up. The bags remain in your car, but the building’s loot resets, allowing you to rinse and repeat. 

Most players agree that this is probably the worst way to experience GTA 6. “Nah I’m good! Didn’t wait 13 years just to glitch my way through the game,” said one fan . 

“Takes away from the experience,” another poster…

items.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall Review
items.summary:
Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall is in select theaters on November 20. 

Paul Thomas Anderson’s concert movie, Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall, is as stripped-back and threadbare as they come in keeping with its subject: a minimalist solo concert by Geese front man Cameron Winter. The twenty-four-year-old folk artist — twenty-three at the time of filming — sits at a piano on a darkened stage, titled away from the audience, creating a gentle mystery of sorts which Anderson complements with his camera, operated on occasion by producer Benny Safdie. The result will no doubt depend on your interest in Winter’s music, but the documentary evokes a grounded tactility that’s hard to ignore, and whose allure is harder to deny.

With the beeps and boops of mobile ticket scanners, Anderson welcomes us inside the titular concert hall (How do you get there? Practice !) before a hard cut from empty stands to a full and bustling crowd creates anticipation. It’s a far cry from the filmmaker’s other concert movie — the Jodhpur-set Junun — which made use of digital tech like drones to gawk at its Indian musicians like animals in a zoo. Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall feels far more compassionate, as though its director either felt closer to the music or had simply reached greater maturity as a documentarian.

The dim concert space comes alive thanks to the grain of Anderson’s 35mm film — across several cameras — creating an image that feels fluid and rhythmic, even in static moments. It feels no less enveloping even when on-screen audience members occasionally display a lack of etiquette…

items.title: GTA 6 is playable in first-person, here's how to activate it
items.summary:
While you can switch to first-person temporarily in Grand Theft Auto 6 when you want to get a real good close-up of a texture or when you're looking at your phone, you can't run around doing crimes and having fun like you could when GTA 5 got its first-person mode. Except actually you can, as discovered by players on Reddit and tested by our own Morgan Park.

It's easy enough to activate in-game. Go to the controller settings, then under the Controller Features section change your touch pad/select button to Camera 2 / 2. Get into a car, bring up your phone with the D-pad, press Circle or B then quickly hit Select. There you go, first-person GTA 6.

As Morgan's footage shows, it's completely playable. It doesn't look 100% done, however, with your shoulders clipping through the camera when you've got a longarm gun up. Seeing someone break into a car in first-person also looks a bit rough around the edges. While conspiracy theorists have convinced themselves that Rockstar is holding back this feature to sell it as DLC, I figure they're probably still polishing it to add in a future update.

If you want to leave first-person, you'll have to reload a save. It doesn't have to be an old save, though. If you save in first-person then immediately load the same save you'll be back in third-person and have to return to God's own preferred viewpoint.

I'm playing the world's most renowned automotive crime fantasy, and I can't stop observing the basic tenets of road safety.

items.title: GTA 6 has the best use of the PS5 controller I've ever seen
items.summary:
Six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing. They're key for Astro Bot's varied trigger-based mechanics, of course, and I wouldn't want to play Death Stranding 2 without my heavy backpack fighting back against me.

But my new favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6.

GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective. The resistive triggers activate when you'd expect, like while shooting guns, but they also come into play in activities that feel like they were designed around the controller: When swinging dumbbells, for instance, the triggers help me time when to release and start another rep. It's cool stuff.

Rockstar's smartest use of the triggers, and one of my favorite new features of GTA 6 in general, is its two-stage throttle for vehicles : When you pull the throttle (right trigger) in any car, there's a hard resistive stop at about the 50% to 60% point.

I've been calling this low-speed mode . At this speed, my car moves at a cruising pace that I find very comfortable—still slightly faster than NPC cars, but slow enough to follow the flow of traffic, take in my surroundings, or easily slam the brakes before running over a grandma on her way home from Canasta. I've also been calling it "normal driving" mode.

items.title: GTA 5's Steam concurrents have gone up rather than down now that GTA 6 is out, suggesting a lot of PC players are waiting
items.summary:
Pour one out for the PC gamers who are now forced to watch everyone frolic in the streets of Grand Theft Auto 6 on consoles this week. The next best thing on PC is GTA 5, and its recent Steam concurrents suggest people are trying their best to fight the FOMO until Rockstar decides to bring the new one over.

You might assume GTA 5 player counts would tank now that it's old news, but the numbers have actually jumped up a bit in the last month. SteamDB shows a peak of around 87,000 concurrent players in the last day, an almost 10% increase from October. There's been a bit of a dip today—which could partially be attributed to GTA 6 finally becoming available in every region—but it's not as sharp of a drop as you'd think it'd be for a 13-year-old game.

In fact, GTA 5 has steadily kept a good amount of players over the last year, with major spikes happening around the occasional price discount. It usually hovers around 40,000 to 50,000 average concurrent players, and GTA 6's release hasn't broken the pattern. That's the beauty of PC gaming for you: Steam sales and mods keep games like this chugging along years after they'd be considered cutting edge.

(Image credit: SteamDB) GTA 5 holdouts might have a long road ahead of them though. GamesBeat reported last month that "four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans" said GTA 6 will make its way to PC in the first three months of 2027. In the past, Rockstar held PC releases back for at least seven months (GTA 5 PC took a year and six months), so an early 2027 release would be unorthodox if the report is true.

items.title: Should you give the statue to Benedict Halifax in GTA 6?
items.summary:
Deciding whether to give the statue to Benedict Halifax is a decision you'll need to make during the fourth story mission of Chapter 3 in GTA 6 , called Dubious Provenance. This mission will kick off after Cal visits the Bayside apartment you're borrowing from Boobie to inspect the hard drive.

Once Cal leaves, you'll see an icon of a statuette at the closet door. Remember, you didn't just acquire a hard drive but a bronze statuette in Chapter 1, and if you interact with it now the mission will begin. First, you need to drive to Capri, a ritzy town on the other side of the map. 

At the antiques store, Evelyn Andrews tells you she isn't interested in the obviously stolen item, but art dealer Benedict Halifax approaches you on the sly and says he can have it appraised for you. Should you give the statue to him?

Give the statue to Halifax : He'll give you a watch to hold onto as collateral while he appraises the statue. Then he'll vanish for a while, trying to duck you, and you'll have to call him repeatedly to track him down again. Don't give the statue to Halifax : This is really just delaying the rest of the mission. You can keep the statue for now, but if you want to progress the mission you'll have to go all the way back to Capri at some point and give it to him anyway. So, you might as well just give it to him. Things shake out the same way no matter what you choose, but not giving it to him just means the mission will ultimately take longer to complete.

items.title: In the GTA 6 Delights robbery mission, help or don't help Frankie and Mario?

You'll face a choice in Chapter 2 of GTA 6 , when you're ready to help Vicky rob her boss, Frankie, at the Delights strip club in Port Gellhorn. Frankie asks you an important question and you've only got a couple seconds to respond:

"Can you dance? Yes or no, dude?" Frankie has caught you (as Jason) coming in the back door of the club as you and Lucia prepare to rob it. It's ladies night and one of the male strippers is out of commission, but Mario, the lead stripper, gets an idea when he meets Jason. Frankie has the same idea, and asks if Jason knows how to dance.

Personally, both versions are worth seeing, but Jason playing a stripper, and Lucia's utter delight at seeing him play a stripper, is way more fun.

items.title: Fact check: Does GTA 6 stop players from shooting inside gay nightclubs and crashing planes into buildings?
items.summary:
As players explore Leonida for the first time, misleading claims about Grand Theft Auto 6 have begun circulating on social media as evidence that Rockstar has toned down the series' violence. The two claims I've seen most often are along the lines of:

"GTA 6 prevents players from shooting inside of a gay nightclub" "GTA 6 makes planes bounce off of buildings to avoid 9/11 references" Both of these claims are misleading half-truths.

Does GTA 6 prevent players from shooting inside of a gay nightclub? ⛔ No, because there is no gay or LGBTQ nightclub in GTA 6. 

(Image credit: Rockstar Games) It is true that you cannot use firearms inside of GTA 6 clubs, such as Nine1nine and The Vault . Grand Theft Auto 5 had the same restriction. But none of the clubs in GTA 6 are specifically presented as gay or LGBTQ clubs.

It is reasonable to speculate that Rockstar would want to avoid in-game scenarios that closely resemble the 2016 Pulse nightclub shooting in Florida—the state Leonida parodies—but the studio has not stated as much.

Do GTA 6 planes just bounce off of buildings? ⛔ No, unless you've turned on a setting which reduces vehicle damage. 

Clips of Grand Theft Auto 6 airplanes smacking into tall buildings without taking any apparent damage have been used on social media to claim that Rockstar is intentionally preventing players from replicating 9/11-like crashes, or that the vehicle physics are shoddy.

The clips of ultra-strong planes aren't fake, but are achieved by turning on "Reduced Vehicle Damage" in the gameplay settings.

items.title: Valve may raise Steam Machine prices yet again: 'Memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels'
items.summary:
Valve has good news and bad news for anyone interested in buying a Steam Machine. All current reservations for the 512GB model have been fulfilled and there's stock remaining, so if you want one you can just head over to the purchase page and buy it—but the 2TB model is in shorter supply so signups for the waitlist are no longer being taken. 

And, sorry to say, there's also worse news: Valve says it won't be able to produce them in the quantities it had planned, and the price could increase.

Despite their high prices, demand for Steam Machines was high enough that Valve implemented a randomized lottery system to buy one: Prospective purchasers signed up for a shot, a randomized selection were put in a reservation queue with a Steam Machine reserved in their name, and everyone else went to the waiting list to be notified when more reservation spots came open.

Valve said in July that it expected to have the reservation queue caught up by the end of 2026 , and that's now the case with the 512GB model: They're in an "an add-to-cart status," meaning that while supplies last, you can purchase one and it will be shipped straight away.

The situation is less happy for people waiting for the 2TB model, though. In an update posted today, Valve said all reservation holders have been sent their invitations to purchase but there are still people on the waiting list; those people won't lose their positions, but no one else will be allowed to join.

items.title: Where to have a bona fide bigfoot (skunk ape) sighting in GTA 6
items.summary:
One of GTA's many gags is back in GTA 6: the ol' bigfoot sighting. Well, technically I think it's a " skunk ape ," real-life Florida's maybe real-life boogeyman "cousin" to Bigfoot. Don't get that cryptid family tree twisted. How do I know it's skunk ape? I saw the thing, I swear, and there was a cloud of green stink wafting off of it. Here's exactly where it's at if you want your own smelly primate encounter.

Bigfoot encounter location in GTA 6 

Look for the dead end road on the west side of this peninsula. (Image credit: Rockstar) The skunk ape sighting I've found so far is just across Gambit Bay from Jason's initial house. Hop in Jason's boat on the dock outside his place and set course for the dead end road on the inside of this peninsula. Before you even make land you'll get a prompt telling you to use Focus Mode to follow the source of the noises.

Hark! It's skunk ape! The creature hightails its stinky hide off into the mangrove-y woods and you'll need to keep using focus mode to chase after. You'll lose sight of it and instead find some creepy effigy thing standing beside a tree. Check it out, get stink-apacitated, and get your not so informative close-up sighting of bigfoot's big feet.

Stinky guy sighted. (Image credit: Rockstar) After your sighting, keep your eyes peeled for flyers about the skunk ape posted on storefronts and telephone poles around Leonida. They'll lead you to a mission where you can learn more about the mysterious beast.

items.title: Your GTA 6 car is your Red Dead 2 horse, and it's perfect
items.summary:
Every time the very concept of a GTA 6 has come up in the past eight years, I've had just one wistful opinion to contribute: "I hope they make it more like Red Dead Redemption 2."

I'm not a huge GTA guy, but I am a Red Dead head. The sequel is Rockstar's best work (maybe second best now?) because of all the ways it prioritizes roleplay and choice-making by simulating the little things: Mixing tonics, crafting bullets individually, grooming Arthur's mustache. God, I love that stuff.

There was no way Rockstar would repeat all of these life sim-y touches for the louder and faster GTA 6, but I am surprised and elated that my favorite Red Dead 2 feature of them all made the cut: Your car is your horse. 

That is to say, Jason and Lucia's personal vehicles are their mobile bases—an essential extension of them. You can't pet or name it, sadly, but it's important to keep track of and take care of your whip, because it's where you keep all your guns and outfits. It's all literally in the trunk: If you want to fetch your shotgun, you have to walk to the back of the car, open it up, and fish it out of a box.

Gone are the days of keeping seven assault rifles, ten SMGs, and four rocket launchers in your back pocket—you can only equip two "long" guns on your back, and large melee weapons like bats have to be stowed away, too. Aside from how cool it is to fish a shotgun out of my trunk like a disgruntled Jason Statham character, the limitation is forcing me to think twice about how to approach missions.

And unlike in Red Dead's lawless towns, the NPCs of Leonida seem to react…
items.t: Your GTA 6 car is your Red Dead 2 horse, and it's perfect

items.title: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world
items.summary:
The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005.

Probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far, clinging to its source like a frightened ghost.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling
items.summary:
I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth , the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.

Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.
items.t: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling

items.title: Korridor turns those Youtube ads for vertical mobile shooters into a new, "deeply strategic" genre, and I can't decide if it's lying
items.summary:
I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters. You know the ones: boglins pour towards an auto-firing player, who must dodge about to grab upgrades while whittling down the horde. The player in the advert always does pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre midboss, and: bam!

Show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.

items.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
items.summary:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r , or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6 's idolising reviews , that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.
items.t: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
